html:
Mohammed Abdullah Hassan was a Somali religious leader and poet who led an armed resistance against British, Italian and Ethiopian rule for about twenty years, from 1899 to 1920. The British called him the "Mad Mullah".

He was a scholar of a Sufi order who had studied in Arabia. Back in the Horn of Africa he preached against the Christian powers then dividing up Somali lands: Britain in British Somaliland, Italy in Italian Somaliland, and Ethiopia under Menelik II to the west. His followers, the Dervishes, built stone forts, the largest at Taleh, and fought off several British expeditions.

He was also one of the great masters of Somali oral poetry. His poems, attacking enemies and rousing followers, are still recited.

In 1920 the British used aircraft of the Royal Air Force together with ground troops to bomb his forts. He escaped into Ethiopia and died there later that year, probably of influenza. In Somalia he is remembered as a national hero.
